core_obligations: Assume the third condition and let a module over the smaller ring be given, and form the cohomology of the derived tensor product against it (proof lines 17193-17197).
Identify the localisations of these cohomology modules with the cohomology of the localised complex against the localised module, so that the hypothesis applies (proof lines 17197-17201).

Apply the criterion that vanishing at all maximal ideals implies vanishing, obtaining the first condition; the two remaining implications are explicitly omitted by the author (proof lines 17201-17206).
proof_roadmap: Form the cohomology and note it is a module over the larger ring (proof lines 17193-17197).
Localise and apply the hypothesis (proof lines 17197-17201).
Conclude by the local vanishing criterion (proof lines 17201-17207).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the tor amplitude of a complex of modules over one ring, computed over a smaller ring, can be tested after localising at the primes or even only the maximal ideals of the larger ring, and the proof is a 15-line argument for the substantive direction. It takes the cohomology of the derived tensor product against an arbitrary module, observes that it is a module over the larger ring whose localisations compute the cohomology of the localised complex against the localised module, and applies the criterion that a module is zero once all its localisations at maximal ideals are zero to conclude vanishing outside the interval. The author states explicitly that the two remaining implications between the three conditions are omitted, and that sentence is reproduced verbatim.
